answer: Cross-epoch behavior ledger. Each identity’s actions are compared with its prior-epoch pattern; only identities staying within tolerance retain standing, while any break resets standing to its nadir. A sybil cluster must run separate persistent histories per identity across epochs, paying per-identity storage, monitoring, and epoch-boundary recomputation that does not amortize. New identities remain unranked until they establish a stable vine of consistent interactions. Recovery after a break also consumes copper, so each duplicate adds recurring cost.
